title: Dynamic attention-kernel evaluator and prefill coalescer to reduce kernel thrash and startup jitter
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Background: We observe intermittent latency spikes and throughput variance driven by oscillation between attention kernel backends (FlashAttention v2, v3, and fallback GEMM/naive shaders) during the prefill -> decode startup phase. Oscillation happens when the kernel selector flips choices across adjacent requests or across prefill and immediate decode segments, causing workspace reallocations and kernel warm/cold penalties. Goal: Implement a lightweight dynamic evaluator that scores candidate attention kernels based on short-window telemetry and coalesce nearby prefill requests to reduce selector churn, while preserving latency SLOs and avoiding regressions on tail latency or memory fragmentation.
plan: 1) Design a scoring function that blends recent P50/P95 latency, observed workspace allocation delta, and successful kernel-run ratio into a kernel score (sigmoid-normalized).
2) Add a short-lived local history (per-model-per-machine) with time-decayed counts (window=30s, decay=exp(-t/15s)).

3) Implement a prefill coalescer that: groups prefill requests arriving within 20ms into a provisional batch for kernel selection; pins kernel choice for the whole batch; marks group warm status for next 200ms.
4) Expose a runtime flag to enable the evaluator and coalescer (flags: attn_eval=on/off, coalesce_ms=20, warm_pin_ms=200).
5) Add telemetry hooks: kernel_decision, kernel_score, workspace_bytes_before/after, group_id, warm_pin_hit. Ship canary to internal staging for 48h.
6) Run benchmarks across representative workloads (chat short-turns, long prefill, multi-message high-throughput) comparing baseline, evaluator-only, coalescer-only, and combined modes.
7) Iterate on score weights and decay constants per profiling evidence. Prepare rollback feature-flag for forced baseline routing.
acceptance_criteria: No increase > 3% in P95 end-to-end prefill+first-decode latency on any benchmarked workload compared to baseline (median across runs).
Token throughput does not drop by more than 2% sustained for 5m during steady-state load compared to baseline.
Workspace fragmentation (peak workspace_bytes - steady workspace_bytes) is reduced by at least 10% on long-prefill workloads.
Telemetry emitted for >99% of routed requests in staging and maps cleanly to dashboard heatmaps (kernel_score, warm_pin_hit).
Canary toggle able to be flipped off and route returns to previous kernel distribution with no orphaned allocations after 2 minutes.
blockers: Need updated FlashAttention v3 ABI shims from infra (blocked by ENG-432021).
Allocation telemetry hook requires a small change in allocator API (allocator-proto bump).
rollout_plan: Stage 1 (dev): unit tests + microbench harness locally (flags default off).
Stage 2 (staging): enable attn_eval+coalesce_ms=20 for 10% of staging capacity for 48h. Collect telemetry and run automated compare jobs.
Stage 3 (canary): ramp to 5% of production traffic for 24h with aggressive monitoring and auto-rollback if P95 regresses > 5%.
Stage 4 (gradual): 5% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% over weeks with configuration tuning between ramps and signed off by perf owners.
Rollback criteria: P95 increase > 5% sustained > 10m OR kernel_error_rate increase > 0.5%.
regression_mitigation: Feature guarded behind flags with immediate teleport rollback (single-command feature off triggers route re-evaluation).
Enable detailed trace mode for affected requests to capture kernel choice and allocation timeline to speed root-cause analysis.
Maintain a fallback that forces prior kernel selector behavior if workspace allocation pattern crosses historical anomaly bands.
Create postmortem checklist and tie to on-call rotation for the first 72h of canary.
notes: Trade-offs: Coalescing small prefill windows reduces kernel churn but may add 10-25ms artificial batching latency for individual prefill arrival within the coalescing window—we target 20ms as a sweet spot after initial profiling.
We must be careful with multi-tenant GPU nodes where coalescing across tenants could violate fairness; the coalescer is per-tenant/per-model by default.
This approach is complementary to longer-term kernel-autotuning (model fingerprinting) efforts; evaluator provides short-term stabilization while autotuner gathers richer signals.
